comparator.name: Mathematics (Wiskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 catalogue and regulations support a 180 EC Mathematics degree taught in Dutch, with some courses in English. This example includes 6 EC of open choice in year one, 12 EC of mathematics electives in each of years two and three, and 30 EC of open study in year three. The required 18 EC project includes a thesis and bachelor seminar presentations.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, coherence, content, distinctness and feasibility gates. The closest route integrates mathematical methods with logic, algorithms, optimisation, probability, statistics and data models. The second uses the explicit science-connection interests to organise a materially different Earth-system and scientific-data route. A third proof-intensive pure-mathematics direction cannot supply cumulative real analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory, number theory, complex analysis, specialist proof seminars or an 18-EC mathematics research project. These omissions remain explicit rather than relabelling adjacent computational or Earth-science work as full Mathematics.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide programming used to implement mathematical work; UCR is a general programming foundation.
Both use sets, logical reasoning and induction. Leiden uses proof to construct number systems and study convergence.
Both establish calculus for mathematical problem solving; UCR also introduces matrices, complex numbers and differential equations.
Both introduce estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests. Leiden derives inference from probability models, while UCR connects it to research design and measurement.
Both study discrete optimisation and linear programming. Leiden emphasises combinatorial algorithms and proofs of correctness. UCR also covers heuristic search and constraints in AI.
Both directly study matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations.
Both develop numerical equation-solving, approximation and error/stability reasoning.
Both analyse linear systems using transforms. UCR concentrates on signals, filtering and feedback, while Leiden develops the theory of ordinary differential equations.
Both establish probability; UCR integrates probability distributions, inference and simulation.
Both extend calculus to functions of several variables. UCR also treats complex-valued functions and differential equations, while Leiden develops multivariable analysis in greater theoretical depth.
Both use Monte Carlo simulation to examine statistical methods. UCR uses it to study sampling distributions and applies estimators to economic data.
UCR has no separate breadth course introducing multiple areas of university mathematics through discipline-specific proof and problem work.
Logic and linear algebra do not reproduce a first abstract-algebra course.
UCR logic and optimisation courses do not reproduce the target’s dedicated combinatorics-and-optimisation component.
Year one allows nonoverlapping courses from Leiden bachelor’s programmes.
Leiden teaches mathematical writing and presentations in a dedicated seminar. UCR develops academic communication in Personal & Professional Development and course projects.
The one scheduled UCR linear-algebra course is already aligned with Linear Algebra 1; the second external course remains visible.
UCR has no topology course.
UCR Advanced Calculus includes complex functions but does not reproduce a dedicated complex-analysis course.
UCR has no measure-theory course.
UCR has no second abstract-algebra course.
UCR has no algebraic-geometry or algebraic-curves course.
Leiden’s seminar takes a practical problem from mathematical formulation through solution and communication. Neither UCR plan includes a dedicated seminar with that remit.
Leiden requires a supervised mathematics project with a thesis and seminar presentations. UCR offers independent research as a separate option.
Year three can include a designated minor, additional mathematics courses or another approved selection.
Leiden’s team project uses differential equations to answer a practical question and report findings. UCR covers some of the mathematical methods.

blocks.title: Pure-mathematics depth, project and open profile

notes.text: The UCR plans share several mathematical and computational methods with Leiden. Leiden develops proof across successive courses in analysis and algebra, teaches topology and measure theory, and requires a supervised mathematics project.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Mathematics degree is taught in Dutch, with some courses in English. It builds from calculus, linear algebra, probability and proof to advanced analysis, algebra, topology and mathematical modelling. Students finish with a supervised research project, a thesis and seminar presentations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR options develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods and probability. One applies these methods to algorithms and statistical models. The other uses them to study Earth systems and environmental data. Leiden offers a deeper sequence in proof and pure mathematics and requires a mathematics research project.
